answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-slash reputation bond: before trading, each agent locks collateral that is forfeited if peers prove it cheated, and released only after a record of verified work. A Sybil attacker must fund a separate bond for every fake identity, so attacking at scale costs as much as the identities are worth, while one honest agent pays once. If Falcon, Lotus, and Yarrow are three real agents, each keeps its own bond and history; a thousand clones of one of them would need a thousand bonds, making mass fakery unprofitable.
